questions.stem: In dialysis, why does the dialysis fluid contain glucose but no urea?

options.text: To feed the patient through their blood during treatment
So that glucose diffuses into the blood while urea diffuses out down its concentration gradient
Because urea would damage the dialysis machine
To replace the glucose that the kidneys normally produce

questions.explanation: The dialysis fluid contains glucose at normal blood concentration so it is not lost from the blood. It contains no urea so that urea diffuses out of the blood down its concentration gradient, effectively removing this waste product.
